# BinFloat Conformance Data

The user-facing semantic claim is summarized in
[`doc/manual/conformance/bin_float.md`](../../doc/manual/conformance/bin_float.md);
this page remains the operational source for corpus provenance and commands.

This directory defines the reproducible, finite conformance gate for the
supported `bin_float` IEEE 754 operations. It deliberately separates a pinned
test contract from the unbounded stress modes offered by TestFloat.

## Commands

```sh
just conformance smoke binary
just conformance fetch binary
just conformance plan binary --level 1 --tininess after --tininess before
just conformance run binary --level 1 --tininess after --tininess before
just gate binary 8
```

`just conformance smoke binary` runs the committed 240-row TestFloat subset,
three hexadecimal sqrt witnesses, 120 MPFR-generated integer-power witnesses,
2,088 full-family elementary witnesses, 1,716 `mpfr_strtofr` witnesses and
3,300 `mpfr_get_str` witnesses without downloading anything.
`just conformance fetch binary` verifies SHA-256 and
installs the external artifacts under `.tmp/`. `just gate binary` builds the reference
generator and the native interpreters, then runs the declared full gate.

## Declared Full Gate

The full TestFloat matrix is finite and deterministic:

- formats: binary16, binary32, binary64, binary128;
- operations: add, subtract, multiply, divide, square root, mulAdd, rem,
  roundToInt, to_i32, to_i64, to_ui32, to_ui64, eq, le, lt, eq_signaling,
  le_quiet, lt_quiet;
- rounding: nearest-even, nearest-away, toward-zero, toward-negative,
  toward-positive, except for rem and the comparisons, which ignore it and run
  once;
- tininess detection: before and after rounding for the arithmetic operations
  and mulAdd, after rounding elsewhere;
- exactness: both `-notexact` and `-exact` for roundToInt and the integer
  conversions;
- TestFloat level: 1, seed: 1.

Its 468 tasks contain 254,227,872 vectors: 7,461,360 for the five arithmetic
operations and 246,766,512 for the IEEE operations (245,329,920 of them
mulAdd). Invalid integer conversions are compared by flags only, because
SoftFloat returns platform-specific sentinels where the API returns `None`. The MPFR part executes every one of
the 1,055 executable rows in the pinned `tests/data/sqrt` file, 1,716
hash-pinned `mpfr_strtofr` cases and 3,300 hash-pinned `mpfr_get_str` cases
(see Decimal Character Conversion below) plus 2,088
hash-pinned cases covering 29 elementary operations, binary32/64/128
precisions, and all six `BinaryRoundingMode` values. The runner
requires exact encoded results and exception bits for non-NaN results. For a
NaN result it requires a quiet NaN class and the exact exception bits, because
IEEE 754 permits implementation choices for a generated NaN payload.

`--level 2` remains available as a much larger, deterministic stress suite.
It is intentionally not part of the published finite gate: it contains tens to
hundreds of millions of vectors per high-precision binary operation. The
runner streams it in bounded chunks, validates that every generated row was
executed, and never truncates or substitutes vectors.

As an additional stress result, the complete binary16 level-2 matrix (all five
operations, five rounding directions, and both tininess modes) executed
50,205,600 / 50,205,600 vectors successfully. This result demonstrates the
streaming path; it does not turn the much larger binary32/64/128 level-2 suite
into a published claim.

## Decimal Character Conversion

IEEE 754-2019 5.12 `convertFromDecimalCharacter` (`BinFloat::from_string_ctx`)
and `convertToDecimalCharacter` (`to_decimal_string_ctx`,
`to_shortest_string`) are checked against two generated MPFR 4.2.2 corpora
(`cc -I<mpfr>/include -L<mpfr>/lib tools/generate_mpfr_decimal_string_oracle.c -lmpfr -lgmp`,
then `generator strtofr 24 20261014` or `generator output 12 20261014`; the
files and digests are pinned in `corpora.json`).

`mpfr-4.2.2-strtofr.txt` (header `mpfr-strtofr-v1`) has one row per literal:
`precision rounding input expected inexact overflow underflow`, with `expected`
the `mpfr_strtofr` result as `[-]0x<hex>p<exp>` (or `inf`, `-0x0p0`). Per
precision (11, 24, 53, 113, 200) and rounding (`n`, `na`, `z`, `u`, `d`, `a`;
`na` is MPFR's nearest-away wrapper) it holds random literals with 1 to 22
mantissa digits and exponents up to ±3·10^8, 60 to 400 digit mantissas, exact
halfway points between adjacent values of the precision and the decimal strings
one unit above and below them, `0`, `-0`, `+5`, `0e999999999`, values next to
the largest binade and literals beyond the exponent range. The runner parses
each literal with `BinFloat::from_string_ctx` and compares value, sign of zero,
and the inexact, overflow and underflow flags.

`mpfr-4.2.2-decimal-output.txt` (header `mpfr-decimal-output-v1`) has two row
kinds. `fixed digits precision rounding value expected_digits
expected_exponent10 inexact` is `mpfr_get_str(base 10, digits)` (no `na`: MPFR
has no nearest-away direction there) compared with `to_decimal_string_ctx`;
`shortest precision value expected_digit_count` is the fewest digits for which
the decimal neighbour below or above the value reads back, to nearest, as the
value, found by MPFR. The runner requires `to_shortest_string` to have exactly
that many significant digits and to read back as the same value with
`BinFloat::from_string`.

Two differences from MPFR shape the corpus. MPFR writes a value as
`0.1xxx × 2^e`, so its largest finite value has the leading bit `2^30 - 2` and
its smallest `-2^30`; `binary_implementation_e_max` and `_e_min` are
`2^30 - 1` and `1 - 2^30` for the leading bit, one binade higher at both ends.
Inputs beyond the range are therefore only included for the rounding directions
that deliver an infinity or a zero in both. And MPFR has no subnormals (it
flushes to its smallest value) where `BinFloat` rounds to a subnormal, so
literals near the underflow threshold are not compared.

## Interpreter Boundary

`src/frontend/testfloat_expr` parses TestFloat rows into typed binary interchange
values, creates the requested `BinaryContext`, and runs `BinFloat` directly.
`src/frontend/mpfr_expr` parses MPFR hexadecimal `data_check` sqrt rows, the
committed `pow_si` rows, the elementary matrix, and the two decimal conversion
corpora. The elementary generator
uses MPFR's required `mpfr_round_nearest_away_begin/end` wrapper rather than
passing the explicitly forbidden `MPFR_RNDNA` value to general functions.
`tools/generate_mpfr_elementary_oracle.c 1852 20260715` produces at least
100,000 fixed-seed cases even for the smallest three-operation family; it is an
optional stress corpus and is not committed. The declared command executed
966,744/966,744 cases successfully. Python only fetches, streams,
shards, and aggregates; it does not implement or alter floating-point
arithmetic.

See the [design](../../doc/manual/design/bin_float.md) and
[conformance](../../doc/manual/conformance/bin_float.md) pages for standards,
algorithms, results, and explicit non-claims.

## Seeded Random Differential Testing

The fixed corpora above use fixed precisions and seeds. The random differential
campaign adds precisions from 2 to 10,000, mixed operand widths, all six
rounding directions, bounded and unbounded exponent ranges, and inputs built to
sit on the edges of rounding, against GNU MPFR 4.2.2. It is driven by
`tools/random_differential.py` (`just random-diff`) and recorded through the
mare_mark harness in `src/differential`; see the
[tutorial](../../doc/manual/tutorial/differential.md) and
[design](../../doc/manual/design/differential.md) pages and
[verification](../../doc/manual/verification.md) for the counts.

```sh
just random-diff smoke
just random-diff run --family add --family elem --count 1000000 --target native --target wasm
just random-diff replay 20261118.add.1234
just random-diff minimize 20261118.exp2.54013 --output testdata/bin_float/random-regressions.txt
```

### Row format (`mpfr-random-v1`)

`tools/generate_mpfr_random_oracle.c <family> <seed> <start> <count>` writes one
row per case:

```
id op rounding precision emin emax tininess a b c n expected flags
```

`id` is `<seed>.<family>.<index>`: a case is a pure function of seed, family and
index (a SplitMix64 stream, integer arithmetic only), so `<family> <seed> I 1`
regenerates row `I` of any run. `op` is one of `add sub mul div sqrt fma
strtofr getstr shortest` or one of the 29 elementary functions of the elementary
matrix (the family `elem` draws one per case, `arith` draws one of the first
six). `rounding` is `n na z u d a` (`na` is MPFR's nearest-away wrapper).
`precision` is the output precision, or the precision of the value for `getstr`
and `shortest`. `emin emax tininess` give the IEEE exponent range (`e_min`,
`e_max`: the smallest normal number is 2^emin, the largest finite value is just
below 2^(emax+1)) and the tininess rule `a` (after rounding) or `b` (before),
or `- - -` for the unbounded context (the implementation limits ±(2^30 − 1) with
gradual underflow). `a b c` are exact operands as `[-]0x<hex>p<exp>`, `inf`,
`-inf`, `nan` or `-`; for `strtofr` `a` is the decimal literal. `n` is the
integer argument (`rootn`, `pown`) or the digit count (`getstr`). `expected` is
the result in the same notation (`<digits>e<exp10>` for `getstr`, the digit count
for `shortest`) and `flags` is `-` or a subset of `xouvz` (inexact, overflow,
underflow, invalid, division by zero). The executor
(`frontend/mpfr_expr`, `parse_random_data`) compares value (including the sign
of zero and of infinity) and flags; a NaN result must be a quiet NaN.

### How the oracle is made to agree with IEEE 754

- **Exponent range.** The generator sets MPFR's range to the row's range plus
  the room needed for subnormals and feeds MPFR only operands inside it, so the
  one-binade difference between MPFR's and BinFloat's limits described above
  does not arise: rows near the implementation limits are compared, not
  filtered.
- **Subnormals.** MPFR has no subnormal numbers. Results in the subnormal range
  go through `mpfr_subnormalize` with the ternary value of the first rounding.
  Round-to-nearest-away has no such mode, so a nearest-away row whose result
  would be tiny is generated in round-to-nearest-even instead.
- **Underflow flag.** Derived from IEEE 754-2019 §7.5 (tiny and inexact), for
  both tininess rules (before rounding: the truncated exact result is below
  2^emin; after: the result rounded to the precision with an unbounded exponent
  is). MPFR's own underflow flag is not used.
- **Invalid and NaN.** MPFR raises its NaN flag for any NaN result; the row
  carries `v` only when no operand is a NaN. NaN operands are never combined
  with a second special operand; NaN payloads are not compared.
- **Operations without a standard answer.** `pow` rows keep a finite base and a
  finite exponent, with an integer exponent for a negative base.

### Known oracle defect: `mpfr_sqrt`

With MPFR 4.2.2 (Homebrew bottle on arm64 macOS, GMP 6.3.0), `mpfr_sqrt` reports
ternary 0, or returns a value on the wrong side of the root, for some operands
whose precision is near the output precision and whose binary exponent is odd.
`tools/mpfr_sqrt_ternary_repro.c` is a standalone reproducer and
`tools/mpfr_sqrt_ternary_search.c` finds more cases. The generator checks every
`sqrt` row with an exact product and draws the case again from the next stream
(the id is unchanged) when MPFR's answer fails; the shard footer
`# oracle-defects-skipped N` counts them. About one row in 100,000 `sqrt` rows
was affected.

### Regression fixtures and the committed sample

- `mpfr-4.2.2-random.txt`: 50 rows per family of seed 20261118 (500 rows),
  regenerated by `just random-diff fixtures`; part of `just random-diff smoke`
  and of `just pr`.
- `random-regressions.txt`: minimized failing cases, each preceded by
  `# xfail #<issue> <note>`. The smoke run requires exactly the annotated rows
  to fail, so a fix is noticed as an unexpected pass and the marker is removed.
